title: Dog-Trade Defenses Need Records Before Reform
excerpt: Claims about dog farms, stolen pets, and poison bait need named records—not repetition. Public safety requires quarantine, transparency, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Every stolen companion animal leaves family loss behind. Yet no police seizure, court judgment, transport interception, or poison-bait incident is identified in the material available for this dispatch. That gap matters: outrage must rest on records, not invented scenes or recycled claims.

Tradition cannot erase missing evidence

“Tradition” does not prove lawful sourcing. “Farm-raised dogs” does not prove farm origin. Those claims require traceable records: breeder or farm registration, transport documents, veterinary certificates, quarantine compliance, and chain-of-custody records. Without them, readers cannot distinguish lawful activity from theft, regulatory breach, or illicit transport.

Biosecurity still demands hard safeguards

Dog-trade supply chains and household rabies exposures are separate issues, but both require competent enforcement. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance states these protections plainly. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route.

Demand records. Demand reform.

Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, and local leaders can demand transparent enforcement without blaming culture or nationality. SDE calls for complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
